description: Job Title: GIS Analyst Job Description The GIS Analyst will support Operation Services, an internal department that aids construction projects. The role involves completing engineering designs and cost estimates using GIS for various main and service works, collecting construction activity 'as-built' data with mobile CPS devices in the field, creating permanent asset records, and editing map features and correlating attribute data in GIS. The analyst will also perform final quality checks on GIS versioned data before posting, represent Engineering at project meetings, and conduct field visits to job sites to determine requirements for service and main work. Responsibilities Complete engineering designs and cost estimates using GIS for all types of main and service work. Collect construction activity 'as-built' using mobile CPS devices in the field for creating permanent asset records. Edit map features and correlating attribute data in the GIS. Perform final quality checks on GIS versioned data before it is posted to the GIS. Represent Engineering at internal and external project meetings as required. Visit job sites to determine requirements for service and main work. Perform preliminary reviews of development plans and interface with customers. Implement and train Engineering staff on new work processes for the GIS mapping system. Distribute and update maps for other departments as requested. Approve requests for the acquisition and release of easements and vacation of rights-of-way. Perform pipeline safety compliance-related GIS analysis as directed. Execute all other duties as assigned. Essential Skills Proficiency in ArcGIS and CAD. Knowledge of geography and construction drawings. Experience with as-built drawings, cost forecasting, and drafting. Additional Skills & Qualifications Ability to complete engineering designs and cost estimates using GIS. Experience in collecting construction activity 'as-built' data using mobile CPS devices. Skill in editing map features and correlating attribute data in GIS. Work Environment The role is based in a professional engineering office, initially requiring attendance five days per week, reducing to three days per week after training. Work may be performed in both office and field settings, with exposure to the elements. Typical hours are 7:00 a.m. to 3:45 p.m., Monday through Friday, with potential for overtime and travel. Pay and Benefits The pay range for this position is $25.00 - $27.00/hr. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to specific elections, plan, or program terms. If eligible, the benefits available for this temporary role may include the following: • Medical, dental & vision • Critical Illness, Accident, and Hospital • 401(k) Retirement Plan – Pre-tax and Roth post-tax contributions available • Life Insurance (Voluntary Life & AD&D for the employee and dependent

Microbiology Lab Analyst Job Description The Microbiology Lab Analyst serves as a Laboratory Technician responsible for performing analytical and microbiological testing on food products, ingredients, and environmental samples to support quality and safety programs. You will apply approved microbiological techniques and methodologies to ensure accurate, reliable results and help maintain compliance with regulatory and customer requirements. Working primarily on second shift, you will prepare and analyze samples, maintain a clean and organized laboratory, monitor and care for equipment, and assist with inventory and quality-related duties. Responsibilities Perform analytical and microbiological testing of food products, ingredients, and environmental samples in accordance with approved methods and protocols. Apply approved microbiological techniques and methodologies to evaluate indicator organisms, pathogens, and relevant chemistries. Prepare and analyze samples for indicator organisms, pathogens, and chemical parameters, ensuring accuracy and proper documentation. Notify laboratory management promptly of any deviations, out-of-specification results, or unusual findings in test results. Maintain appropriate inventory levels of reagents, media, consumables, and supplies required for testing activities. Provide routine preventive maintenance, basic troubleshooting, and thorough cleaning of laboratory equipment to ensure reliable operation. Support quality-related duties, including performing temperature checks, monitoring controls, and verifying proper storage conditions. Adhere to company policies, procedures, and customer requirements while following relevant regulatory and industry guidelines. Maintain a clean, organized, and safe laboratory environment using proper aseptic techniques and good laboratory practices. Stay current with scientific literature, emerging technologies, and industry trends related to food microbiology and analytical testing. Accurately record, interpret, and report test results in accordance with laboratory documentation standards. Collaborate with colleagues and other departments to support continuous improvement in laboratory processes and quality systems. Essential Skills Bachelor's degree in biology, chemistry, or a closely related science field. At least 2 years of experience in a commercial food-testing or analytical laboratory. Hands-on experience with microbiological testing of food products, ingredients, or environmental samples. Proficiency in aseptic sampling techniques and routine laboratory procedures. Knowledge of laboratory equipment operation, care, and basic troubleshooting. Familiarity with Good Laboratory Practices (GLP). Working knowledge of OSHA safety requirements in a laboratory environment. Experience with FDA, BAM, APHA, ISO, or USP methods relevant to microbiology or analytical testing. Ability to follow detailed protocols and standard operating procedures accurately. Strong attention to detail

Job Title: Supply Chain Analyst Job Description The Supply Chain Analyst will play a central role in a small, stable supply chain function, taking on the majority of day‑to‑day supply chain activities and enabling a senior consultant to focus on corporate governance and legal responsibilities. This is a broad, operational role covering contractor and contract management, inventory management, procurement, and bidding, with limited involvement in logistics. It is well suited to someone who enjoys hands‑on operational work, values stability, and is comfortable in a lean, flat organizational structure with modest upward mobility. Responsibilities Manage a broad range of operational supply chain activities, including inventory management, contracts, procurement, and bidding processes. Administer and maintain operational contracts, with a particular focus on Master Service Agreements (MSAs) and related contractor arrangements. Support contractor and contract management activities, ensuring agreements are up to date, compliant, and aligned with operational needs. Coordinate procurement activities, including sourcing, evaluating bids, and selecting suppliers in accordance with internal guidelines. Monitor inventory levels and support inventory management processes to ensure materials and equipment are available for operational needs. Collaborate with various operational departments within a production environment to understand their supply chain requirements and priorities. Perform administrative tasks related to supply chain operations, recognizing that the role is primarily operational rather than focused on large, strategic procurement deals. Work closely with the existing supply chain consultant to assume approximately 80% of current supply chain duties and ensure continuity of processes. Contribute to the ongoing build‑out of the supply chain function within a small team, helping to improve processes while remaining flexible and hands‑on. Operate effectively within a lean department of approximately one to one‑and‑a‑half full‑time supply chain staff, taking ownership of day‑to‑day responsibilities. Essential Skills 3–5 years of experience in a supply chain role Demonstrated experience across a broad range of supply chain functions, including inventory management, contracts, procurement, and bidding. Hands‑on experience working with Master Service Agreements (MSAs) in an operational supply chain context rather than solely on project‑based contracts. Experience in the oil and gas industry, with a basic understanding of how operational departments function within a production company. Comfort with a role that offers limited upward mobility and has a strong administrative and operational focus, without expectation of leading large, strategic procurement deals.
